⎿  boundary.csv: 7 rows, 3 months, 0 duplicates, 0 transfers, 0 uncategorised, 0 recurring
● Confirmed. I'll move the rules into a file you edit, and add a weekly summary
  beside the monthly one.

● Before I write it, here is the shape I have in mind. I have sketched it into
  the tree so you can see where each piece would live and say what you want
  kept.

  · Rule settings. Every value the rules read, in one file you edit rather
    than constants spread through the modules.
  · Statement periods. The month lined up on the date a payment was made,
    the week on the date the bank posted it.
  · Weekly spending summary. The same summary at a finer grain, written
    beside the monthly one rather than over it.
  · One change to the summary itself. A merchant nothing matches is filed
    under one name, counted, and reported in the line at the end, rather
    than sitting among the categories you wrote rules for.

propose.title: Rule settings
propose.description: Gathers every value the rules read, meaning the merchant patterns, what happens to a merchant nothing matches, and which date each summary is lined up on, into one file the reader edits instead of constants spread through the modules. Nothing supplies a default for a missing value, so a file with a piece missing stops the run and says which piece.
propose.rationale: plan: the categories cannot be managed without editing the source while each module owns its own constants

propose.title: Statement periods
propose.description: Decides which period a transaction belongs to, for a month and for a week. The month is lined up on the date the payment was made and the week on the date the bank posted it, because the two are read for different reasons. A month answers what was spent in January, and a week is read next to the statement the bank sends.
propose.rationale: plan: a finer grain than a month needs a period the summary can be grouped by

propose.title: Weekly spending summary
propose.description: The same summary at a finer grain, grouped into weeks and written beside the monthly one rather than over it, so both are readable at once. Recurring payments stay counted in months whichever summary is being read, because that is about when a commitment falls.
propose.rationale: plan: the request is to see spending at a finer grain than a whole month

propose.title: Monthly spending summary
propose.description:
Adds the transactions up into category totals for each period, and reports what it did with the rest in one line at the end: how many rows it read, what it dropped as duplicates, what it treated as transfers, how many it could not categorise, and which payments look recurring. Every one of those choices is read from rules.toml now rather than from a constant of its own.

The policies still run before the adding up, so the totals and the line underneath them are telling the same story, and reordering that changes the numbers. The rows under a period heading are the categories the reader wrote rules for. A merchant nothing matches is counted in the line at the end rather than listed among them, because the bucket is not a category anybody chose.
propose.rationale: plan: the summary reads its settings from rules.toml, and the bucket is reported in the count line rather than among the reader's own categories
